segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so on Northline, they’re still at 42 seats, annual prepay, $54,600 before the services line. They want the September 14 go-live, which is tight but workable.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay. Is the pricing exception still the only blocker?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Mostly. I’ve pinged deal desk Monday and again this morning for the 8% discount sign-off, and the order form is basically parked until they answer.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Got it. Did customer push back on the services fee?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: A little. They accepted the $6,800 onboarding if we can split it into two invoices, one at signature and one thirty days after launch. I nudged finance for that billing approval, because procurement won’t release the PO until they confirm it’s okay.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Makes sense. What about security? Last note I saw was their IT director wanted the data retention language cleaned up.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, legal sent the redline Friday. I’ve been checking with our security team for the final response on the subprocessor question; customer won’t countersign while that’s open.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: So next step is just get those back and send clean paper?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah. If deal desk, finance, and security come back today, I can send the revised order form by 4:00. Otherwise it probably slips past their August 9 purchasing cutoff.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay, keep the close plan updated in the CRM. If it’s still quiet after lunch, I can ask Martin to lean in on the internal approvals.
